G.63 square, oblong, rhombus, and rhomboid

Of quadrilateral figures, a square is equilateral and right-angled; an oblong is right-angled but not equilateral; a rhombus is equilateral but not right-angled; a rhomboid has opposite sides and angles equal but is neither equilateral nor right-angled.

G.79 Pythagorean theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the two legs (Pythagorean Theorem).

G.80 converse of the Pythagorean theorem

G.88 bisected and extended segment

G.94 law of cosines obtuse

In obtuse-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the obtuse angle is greater than the squares on the sides containing the obtuse angle by twice the rectangle contained by one of the sides about the obtuse angle, namely that on which the perpendicular falls, and the segment cut off outside by the perpendicular towards the obtuse angle.

G.95 law of cosines acute

In acute-angled triangles the square on the side subtending the acute angle is less than the squares on the sides containing the acute angle by twice the rectangle contained by one of the sides about the acute angle, namely that on which the perpendicular falls, and the segment cut off within by the perpendicular towards the acute angle.
theorem proof plane-geometry geometric-algebra book-ii point segment angle triangle acute-angled-triangle square acute-angle contained-rectangle straight-line perpendicular plane-angle rectangle

G.144 point taken outside

G.309 square numbers there

G.313 there many numbers

If there be as many numbers as we please in continued proportion, and each by multiplying itself make some number, the products is proportional; and, if the original numbers by multiplying the products make certain numbers, the latter is proportional.

G.314 square measure square

If a square measure a square, the side will also measure the side; and, if the side measure the side, the square will also measure the square.
theorem proof number-theory proportions book-viii point square part-aliquot square-number multiply proportional ratio

G.316 square number measure

If a square number do not measure a square number, neither will the side measure the side; and, if the side do not measure the side, neither will the square measure the square.

G.324 numbers continued proportion

G.326 numbers ratio square

G.337 many numbers please

If as many numbers as we please beginning from an unit be in continued proportion, the third from the unit is square, as will also those which successively leave out one; the fourth is cube, as will also all those which leave out two; and the seventh is at once cube and square, as will also those which leave out five.

G.338 many numbers please

If as many numbers as we please beginning from an unit be in continued proportion, and the number after the unit be square, all the rest is square. And, if the number after the unit be cube, all the rest is cube.

G.339 many numbers please

If as many numbers as we please beginning from an unit be in continued proportion, and the number after the unit be not square, neither will any other be square except the third from the unit and all those which leave out one. G.389 there unequal segments
